alpaca.types: Alpaca comes in two fleece types: Huacaya, dense and crimped, and Suri, with straight, lustrous locks. Peru's technical standard NTP 231.301 classifies sorted fiber by fineness and minimum average length: Baby at about 23 microns or finer (65 mm), Fleece 23.1 to 26.5 microns, Medium Fleece 26.6 to 29, Huarizo 29.1 to 31.5, Gruesa above 31.5, and Corta for short fiber of about 20 to 50 mm. Baby names a fineness class, not the animal's age, so fine fleece from adults can qualify. Processors also sell 'royal' or 'royal baby' lots, their own designation for the finest fiber, commonly described as under about 20 microns. Natural colors run from white through fawns and browns to greys and black, and color is sorted along with grade.
alpaca.fabrics: Huacaya is mostly spun into lofty knitting yarn for sweaters, hats, throws and blankets, including brushed yarns with a soft halo. Suri is usually combed and worsted-spun, giving drapey, lustrous woven suiting, coating and scarves, often blended with silk or fine wool. Because alpaca yarn is less elastic than crimpy wool, it is frequently blended with merino for shape memory, or with nylon for strength in socks. Coarser grades go into rugs, felts, insoles and upholstery. Undyed natural-color yarns are a notable product line, since the fiber arrives in many shades.
alpaca.quality: Ask which grade or micron was used: Baby alpaca suits next-to-skin knits, while Fleece and coarser grades belong in outerwear, throws and rugs. Prickle rises with coarse and medullated fibers, so visible stiff, straight, chalky-white hairs in a soft-looking knit are a warning sign. Drape a knit over your hand and stretch it lightly; alpaca has less elastic recovery than wool, so heavy, loose knits can grow, and a dense gauge or wool blend helps. Check percentages: 'alpaca blend' may be mostly acrylic or wool. Brushed yarns can shed at first. If a product claims Responsible Alpaca Standard certification, the certificate should cover that product.
pros: Natural shades from white to black allow undyed yarns.
Suri gives luster and drape that crimped wools do not.
Alpaca fleece carries relatively little grease, so scouring is simpler than for greasy Merino fleece.
Lofty Huacaya yarns make warm, light knits.
cons: Low elasticity lets heavy knits stretch and sag.
Poorly sorted lots contain coarse, medullated fibers that prickle.
Brushed yarns shed and can felt at friction points.
Grade names such as baby are easily misread as the animal's age.
Moth larvae attack it like other keratin fibers.
alpaca.impact: Peer-reviewed life cycle data for alpaca fiber are scarce, so claims that alpaca has a lower footprint than wool or cashmere should be treated as unquantified unless a study is cited. One relevant measurement exists: in respiration chambers, a 2014 study of alpacas, llamas and Bactrian camels on an alfalfa diet found about 0.32 liters of methane per kilogram of body mass per day, versus about 0.58 in literature data for roughage-fed ruminants, but no significant difference per unit of digestible fiber eaten; camelids simply eat less relative to their size. Much Andean fiber comes from high-altitude herding households, so price paid for raw fleece and grading fairness matter socially. Natural colors reduce dyeing. The Responsible Alpaca Standard covers welfare and land management where certified.
alpaca.care: The care label governs. Hand wash in cool water (about 30 C or below) with a wool detergent free of enzymes and bleach, or use a wool cycle only if permitted. Support the wet garment, press water out without wringing, roll in a towel and dry flat, easing it to shape; never hang a wet alpaca knit, because it stretches. Do not tumble dry. Steam or press at the two-dot setting (up to 150 C) through a cloth, and steam brushed yarns rather than pressing them flat. Fold knits for storage instead of hanging them, keep them clean in sealed or breathable bags, and check for moth larvae. Remove pills gently with a comb.
faq: Baby alpaca is a fineness class, not an age. Under Peru's NTP 231.301 classification it covers fiber of about 23 microns or finer with a minimum average length, and it can come from adult animals with fine fleece. Some processors sell even finer 'royal' lots, which is their own designation.

No reliable general ranking exists. Warmth depends mainly on fabric thickness, trapped air and construction rather than the fiber name. Some alpaca fibers are partly hollow (medullated), but medullation is concentrated in coarser grades that are less used next to skin. Compare garments of similar weight and density instead.
Why does my alpaca sweater stretch?

Alpaca has little crimp and less elastic recovery than wool, so the weight of a knit, especially when wet, pulls it longer. Dry it flat, fold it for storage and choose dense knits or merino blends for heavy garments. Light steaming and reshaping can partly restore the fit.
notable: Under Peru's alpaca standard, the Baby class is defined by fineness and length, so fleece shorn from an adult alpaca can be sold as baby alpaca.
Alpacas, llamas and Bactrian camels produced less methane per kilogram of body mass than roughage-fed ruminants in a 2014 chamber study, but about the same per unit of digestible fiber eaten.
The Peruvian standard sets a minimum average fiber length for each class, 65 mm for Baby and 70 mm for the coarser classes, alongside diameter.
